auditor_value: Assertion false, Reason true (standard A–R scheme option 4). Even the full velocity vector changes by only g×1 s = 10 m/s each second, and |Δspeed| ≤ |Δv| = 10 m/s, so a 20 m/s change of speed per second is impossible; speed is a scalar whose per-second change varies (−g sinφ).

findings.quote: If the Assertion is false but the Reason is true.
findings.note: The verdict text happens to be right, but the solution solves a different problem from the one served: the served Assertion claims a change of 20 m/s per second, and no step, equation or mistake entry ever mentions 20 m/s — every line argues against a 10 m/s claim. A solution that ignores the one number the question gives is graded here as required by the brief; the served claim is false for a stronger reason the solution never states (even the velocity vector changes by only 10 m/s per second).

findings.quote: its change from one second to the next is not a fixed 10 m/s
findings.note: This question's Assertion says 20 m/s, not 10 m/s. The line refutes a claim the served question does not make and leaves the actual claim unaddressed.
findings.fix: Because speed combines both components through a square root, its change from one second to the next is not a fixed value, and it can never be 20 m/s: the whole velocity vector changes by only g × 1 s = 10 m/s each second, so the speed can change by at most 10 m/s in a second, and by less than that whenever the velocity is not vertical.

findings.quote: Confusing velocity with speed, so a constant 10 m/s change in the velocity vector is wrongly read as a constant 10 m/s change in speed.
findings.note: For the served question this cause cannot produce option 1: a student who confuses speed with velocity still sees a 10 m/s per second change, not the 20 m/s the Assertion claims, and so would still call the Assertion false.
findings.fix: Taking the acceleration g = 10 m/s² to mean that the speed changes by 20 m/s over the two halves of every second, or doubling the 10 m/s change without reason, and so accepting the Assertion as true.
